tested_chain: pre-score contracted ADMIT -> runtime-bound RESERVE -> one scorer invocation -> bound SLOT -> exact COMMIT -> provenance-aware CLOSE -> restart/replay
tested_contracts: Every nonempty partial ADMIT/RESERVE/SLOT/COMMIT/CLOSE frame cut used the same length+SHA256 append-frame contract as the durable evaluation journals and was rejected as a clean complete append.
A torn SLOT cannot be scientifically closed; after truncation to the last valid prefix the reserved slot is fail-closed rather than re-run.
A complete bound SLOT with missing COMMIT is reconcilable from the durable SLOT and reservation identity without a second scorer invocation.
A torn CLOSE produces zero reporting rows; only the complete provenance-aware CLOSE commits one row, and restart reproduces the same scientific block score.
A contracted ADMIT cannot be downgraded to the historical compliance CLOSE binding.
Historical ADMITs remain outside this new predicate and are not retroactively reinterpreted.
scope_limitations: The 4531-cut campaign used a deterministic contract-faithful injected runtime with the actual persisted event field structure and frame codec, not byte execution of every frozen production sibling module in one local repository checkout.
The campaign verifies single-writer crash/replay behavior only; it does not establish cross-process mutual exclusion or fencing.
No claim extends beyond reservation authorization provenance, fail-closed evidence inclusion, and the tested append/replay lifecycle.
